pattern.short_summary: The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other.
pattern.definition: The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other. Typically the user commits to a position first and the model's position is then revealed, with a further step in which the user may revise. The juxtaposition, and the divergence it exposes, is the designed object.
pattern.structural_signature: Two verdicts over the same item are held in the interface — one produced by the user, one by the system — and are displayed in the same view or in a fixed temporal order (user commits, system reveals, user re-decides). A revision affordance follows the reveal, and the difference between the two verdicts is itself rendered or computed.

dimension.category_description: How evidence, internals, correspondence, quality, interpretations, and planned actions are represented for human judgment.
dimension.classification_boundary: The representation must support understanding or verification, rather than merely render output into a usable medium.
